turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: Good morning, Elaine. Marcus Lim here, calling for our arranged appointment. Are you somewhere comfortable to speak? Before we get into the review, I'll do the routine identity check.

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: Morning, Marcus. Yes, I'm in my office with the door closed, so now is fine. My NRIC is S five seven seven zero five eight eight G. My date of birth is the fifteenth of November nineteen ninety-four.

turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: Thank you, Elaine. I'll keep the conversation straightforward. I've got your appointment notes in front of me, and we can cover the review first, then sort out future telephone arrangements.

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: That suits me. I've put aside some time before my next meeting. The holding I want you to transact in is Summit Global Equity ETF. I want to sell that holding. The quantity I want to transact is 250 units. Please use US dollars as the currency for this transaction. The amount I'm specifying for this transaction is 50,000. Please place it as a market order.

turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: So your investment objective is to reduce your global equity exposure and free up cash for your planned personal commitments. For Summit Global Equity ETF, falling global equity markets can reduce the value of its underlying holdings. When you sell, price movements or weaker trading liquidity can also mean you receive a less favourable price than the latest quote. Do you understand that falling equity markets can lower the holding's value, and that the actual sale price may be less favourable than the latest quote?

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: Yes, I understand both risks: the holding can fall with equity markets, and the price I actually receive may be below the latest quote.

turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: The transaction fee for this sale is 0.2% of the sale value. You could lose some or all of the capital you invested in this holding. Selling below your purchase price would crystallise that loss. Are you willing to accept an investment loss if this sale crystallises a loss on your holding?

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: Yes, I'm willing to accept that investment loss. I'd rather reduce my exposure than keep waiting for a recovery.

turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: I recommend reducing your holding in Summit Global Equity ETF because that lowers your exposure to global equity volatility and frees up cash for your planned commitments. Please confirm your final instruction: sell 250 units of Summit Global Equity ETF using a market order, with the transaction currency as US dollars and the stated transaction amount as 50,000. Is that your instruction?

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: Yes, I confirm that is my final transaction instruction. Please proceed as you have just stated.

turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: Thank you, Elaine. Before we finish, you mentioned you'd be travelling soon. How would you prefer us to arrange future calls while you're away?

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: I'm going to Japan with my family next month. We'll be moving between a few places, so please send me an appointment message first rather than calling unexpectedly.

turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: Certainly. We can use the usual appointment channel. Would you prefer to leave the next appointment until you're back, rather than fitting a call around the trip?

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: Yes, after I'm back is better. I don't want to be taking calls while we're on a train or trying to find the hotel. I'll message when I'm settled.

turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: That's fine. For appointments back in Singapore, is the morning generally easier, or would an afternoon slot work better with your office schedule?

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: Late morning usually works best. My staff handle the opening routine, and afternoons tend to fill up with supplier meetings. Just give me a bit of notice.

turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: I'll note that preference for scheduling. Enjoy the family trip, Elaine, and thank you for making time today.

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: Thanks, Marcus. Good to get the appointment done before the office gets busy. Have a good day. Bye.
